articles.headline: Source: Packers lose DT Javon Hargrave for season to torn Achilles
articles.description: Tests confirmed Monday that Packers defensive tackle Javon Hargrave suffered a season-ending torn Achilles in Sunday's victory over the Bears, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- For the second time in as many games, the Green Bay Packers lost a defensive player to a season-ending torn Achilles. This time, it's veteran defensive tackle Javon Hargrave.

A source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that tests on Monday confirmed that Hargrave suffered the same fate as linebacker Edgerrin Cooper did a week earlier.

Hargrave was injured in the final minutes of Sunday's 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears. At the end of a pass rush move, he came up hopping and couldn't put any weight on his right leg. He was eventually carted off the field.

"Obviously really excited for our team and winning the game, but I just saw Hargrave and it doesn't look good," coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. "That kind of takes the air out of the room a little bit, when you lose such a, just not only a great player but a great guy, a key piece to this team, and it kind of puts a little bit of a cloud on the day."

The Packers signed the 33-year-old Hargrave to a two-year, $23 million contract in free agency this offseason. It included a $10.5 million signing bonus. Hargrave played in four of the first five games this season, missing Week 2 against the New York Jets because of a knee injury and a concussion. While he did not start any of the games, he played 123 defensive snaps and was credited with four tackles.

Including Hargrave, the Packers had six defensive tackles on the roster. They also have Warren Brinson on injured reserve because of calf and groin injuries and Jordon Riley on the physically unable to perform list because of the Achilles tear he sustained last season. It's possible that one or both could be back this season.

articles.headline: Samaje Perine gives Bengals a strong jolt to end 2-game skid
articles.description: When the run game was struggling, the Bengals turned to Perine, whose downhill style paid dividends.
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Early in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins, the Cincinnati Bengals realized what was going on with the run game wasn't working.

So like they have in previous years, they decided to try something different -- yet familiar.

Enter Samaje Perine. With Cincinnati's run game faltering again, the Bengals used a scheme that fit his strengths -- attacking the line of scrimmage and going downhill.

And it worked. One week after getting stuffed against the Jaguars, Cincinnati was much better on the ground in a 31-24 victory. At a time in the season when the Bengals are trying to find their identity, they might have found the solution.

"The coaches challenged the [offensive] line to create space," Perine said. "And they created a lot of space, and we just had to run."

Perine downplayed any schematic changes Cincinnati (3-2) made to fix the ailing run game, but the numbers tell a different story.

According to ESPN Research, 36.7% of the called runs were classified as inside zone calls. That is the third-highest rate of inside zone Cincinnati has called since ESPN started tracking that data in 2024. Conversely, the Bengals used outside zone on 10% of its rushing calls, their fourth-lowest rate in a game over the past three seasons. To be more precise, the Bengals used what could be called a "midzone" rushing scheme that attacked the middle of the line of scrimmage.

And Perine was the one who benefited. Coming into Sunday, he had a combined 13 carries in the previous four games. But against the Dolphins (0-5), Perine tallied a season-high 14 carries for 68 yards and also had a receiving touchdown as the Bengals snapped a two-game losing streak.

Bengals center Ted Karras said that the offensive line did a good job of moving Miami's defensive tackles and then blocking the linebackers, which opened up downfield rushing lanes for Perine and starter Chase Brown.

Brown, who has been the team's entrenched starter since the 2024 season, was bottled up early in Sunday's game. In the first half, he averaged just 2.4 yards per carry while Perine was at 6.1 yards.

As the game went on, the numbers evened out. Not only did Perine and Brown have a nearly identical split in the number of subsequent carries (seven for Perine, six for Brown), but their rushing average per attempt was nearly identical (3.6 at Perine, 3.7 for Brown).

Moving forward, Bengals coach Zac Taylor said the offense will approach the rushing plan on a week-to-week basis for whatever is needed for the team to score. But he had a glowing endorsement of the way Cincinnati's top two running backs split backfield duties.

"Sometimes you have two great backs that you've got trust in," Taylor said. "That's just the way it can go sometimes, and I don't think there's anything wrong with that."

The win at Hard Rock Stadium highlighted one of the team's more unheralded players over the years.

Perine, 31, is in his third stint with the Bengals. He first joined the club in 2019

articles.headline: Windhorst: Why Cooper Flagg's ascension is starting to feel inevitable
articles.description: The NBA China Games showcased Cooper Flagg's evolving game, leadership and, perhaps most impressive, his franchise-savior ceiling.
articles.body:
MACAO, China -- A few Dallas Mavericks veterans have been keeping up the ruse that Cooper Flagg is still wearing some sort of "trainee" name tag. That the 2025 No. 1 pick is technically a rookie until he plays the first game of his second season.

This played out with various menial duties for the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year -- bag-carrying and the like -- during the team's week in China for two preseason games against the Houston Rockets. "I can sometimes sneak by without them remembering that they want me to be a rookie still. But yeah, they definitely try," Flagg said.

This notion, of course, is ridiculous on its face. Flagg played just 45 minutes in two games in Macao but scored 33 points with 10 rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and two blocks. He hunted for his shot and looked to set up his teammates with the kind of assurance that obliterates the concept that he's a rookie. 

But it's not just what you can count or see. Flagg's voice echoed through the arena inside The Venetian Macao, and he's vocally involved in the game, showing how quickly he is graduating from worrying about his own game to broadening his scope by including everyone else's. He's barreling down the runway toward superstardom like the many fully loaded cargo jets taking off from the adjacent Hong Kong International Airport.

This kind of growth creates goosebumps.

"I'm just finding my voice," Flagg said. "Being so young and a little bit inexperienced is tough sometimes, but I think up to this point, I've earned the respect of my teammates, and I've gotten that sense that they really respect me and my opinion."

For a player who has been on the basketball world's radar since he was 16, was a star at Duke and then won the NBA's top rookie honor, it feels possible that Flagg's quickening maturation might be a tad underrated at the moment. It doesn't help that the Mavericks, mired in a deep Western Conference, aren't exactly demanding attention.

But everything about Flagg is starting to feel inevitable.

There's a lot going on in the NBA: LeBron James is in Philadelphia. Giannis Antetokounmpo is in Miami. Victor Wembanyama has claimed the unofficial "future face of the league" designation and is looking for revenge after Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks, the big-market darlings, grabbed rightful attention by ending their 52-year title drought.

But for a week in Macao for the NBA's China Games, Flagg was the headliner. His image was plastered on the side of buildings and the focus of a big shoe event. Inside one of Macao's glittering high-end, marble-wrapped malls, he unveiled his personal New Balance logo (his initials combined with the silhouette of a pine tree, a nod to his home state of Maine).

articles.headline: Lille consider legal action after Tiago Santos ruptures ACL in tackle
articles.description: Champions League club Lille said Monday they are considering legal action over an injury to defender Tiago Santos who is set to miss the rest of the season.
articles.body:
Champions League club Lille said Monday they are considering legal action over an injury to defender Tiago Santos, who is set to miss the rest of the season.

The 24-year-old right back ruptured the ACL in his right knee, the club confirmed, in an "uncontrolled and dangerous" tackle Saturday by a Le Havre player during the Ligue 1 game.

Lille did not identify Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson, who was not shown a yellow or red card for the challenge.

It is a second ACL injury for Portugal Under-21 international Santos who damaged his left knee in October 2024.

Lille said they asked the French league and federation to explain the video review process by Saturday's match officials analyzing the incident. The club suggested the tackle justified a direct red card.

"The circumstances of the incident and the lack of any sanction raise serious questions for the club," Lille said, adding they have asked the league to refer the incident to its disciplinary panel.

Lille are second in Ligue 1 after beating Le Havre 1-0 and play at Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Santos played the full game in Lille's opening 3-2 loss at home to Real Betis five weeks ago.

articles.headline: Steven Gerrard says Man City must be stripped of titles after guilty verdict: 'Make them suffer'
articles.description: Steven Gerrard has said that Manchester City "have to be stripped" of their titles after the club were found guilty of 100+ charges of financial misconduct by the Premier League.
articles.body:
Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has said that Manchester City "have to be stripped" of their titles after the club were found guilty of 100+ charges of financial misconduct by the Premier League, adding that an "example must be set"  after their breaches.

The charges against City relate to the years 2009-18, with Gerrard leaving Liverpool in 2015 and famously captaining the side that finished runners-up to City in the league in the 2013-14 season.

City deny all wrongdoing and have appealed the verdict. 

Asked what he felt City's punishment should be, Gerrard did not hold back, saying they must be made to "suffer," like they have done to other teams during the alleged time period. 

"In terms of how I feel, I potentially could be affected if you like, I wouldn't want individual players to give stuff back, that wouldn't be right," Gerrard told The Overlap.

"But the club, they have to be stripped... There needs to be an example set, historically whether that's a star throughout all the years of their achievements, because then it doesn't matter whether the titles are stripped or not, as soon as that star is there, then everyone knows that [success] happened because of what we all know happened. 

"And then there needs to be a punishment moving forward, I don't know what the right one is... I don't think its fair on the Championship if they go down, because they will be one of the three teams that come up, so that takes a slot away from the Championship so it's not fair on the EFL.. Or the teams playing against City week in, week out.

"I think it's more moving forward in the Premier League, to punish them over a period of time, multi-year punishment, that would be my opinion, I'm not saying that's the right opinion but that's just how I feel.

"I think it needs to be a transfer ban, a points [deduction] over a period of time and make them suffer like they've made everyone suffer over the nine, ten years that they've done it. 

"They were strong with Everton, strong with Forest [punishments for breaches]. Good luck to the Premier League but they have to be strong."

While Gerrard has played down the prospect of receiving a retrospective Premier League medal, he has said that those at City must face the consequences of what they've done, if they are proven guilty at the end of the appeal process. 

"It's not personal for me in terms of the Man City players, because they're all outstanding players, they've lived the moment and they deserved it [trophies]" he added.

"I'm not someone who's going to sit here and say I would accept a Premier League medal or I want one that they've got. It wouldn't feel the same, it wouldn't be the same.

articles.headline: Can the Seahawks overcome their turnover problem? 'We're not panicking'
articles.description: Seattle has committed the fifth-most turnovers in the NFL so far this season -- and it cost the team a win Sunday.
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl LX despite a turnover problem that plagued them for most of the 2025 regular season. It's again an issue in 2026 -- and on Sunday, it was the difference.

Two more Darnold interceptions and two more lost fumbles by their short-handed backfield doomed the Seahawks in a 33-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field. Three of those turnovers turned into 21 points for the 49ers, who snapped the Seahawks' nine-game home winning streak and dropped the defending champions to 3-2, two games behind San Francisco in the NFC West standings.

The Seahawks have turned the ball over nine times in five games, which is tied for fifth most in the NFL. That includes three turnovers in their Week 3 loss to the previously winless Washington Commanders.

"We need to grow quickly in terms of complementary football," coach Mike Macdonald said. "Definitely [in] taking care of the football. Way too many giveaways at this point in the season."

For the second week in a row, Darnold was intercepted on Seattle's opening possession. He was trying to hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a third-down throw toward the sideline when 49ers cornerback Renardo Green picked it off. Green got him again on Seattle's first drive of the third quarter, when he jumped in front of a throw over the middle to tight end Elijah Arroyo that didn't have enough air under it.

Darnold was sacked five times -- his most in 24 games with Seattle (including playoffs), per ESPN Research -- and did well to keep several plays alive amid a barrage of pressure.

"There's a couple of decisions that I would like back," said Darnold, who completed 18 of 29 attempts for 195 yards and a touchdown. "The second one that I threw, just being able to kind of throw that over the top and let him go get it. I think the other one is just poor decision. Just got to continue to trust myself, trust my feet, trust what I'm seeing, which I'm doing. But just got to be better taking care of the football."

Darnold has thrown five interceptions since he returned from a glute injury, compared to zero turnovers by Drew Lock while he filled in for most of the first two games. Darnold led all players with 20 turnovers during the 2025 regular season, though he didn't give the ball away in three playoff games despite playing through an oblique injury.

"We're not panicking or anything like that," Macdonald said. "We're just going through what we do every day. I think if we become more efficient and more effective as an offense, that's going to help our quarterback, too. I think it's everybody. It's not just Sam. Sam knows. It's not like he wants to turn it over. We need to just play collectively more efficient. I think when that happens, then the ball doesn't become in jeopardy as much."

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta defends Arsenal after Piero Hincapié, Martin Zubimendi injuries
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal's training programme after confirming Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi suffered "far from ideal" injuries in a post-match session on Saturday.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal's training programme after confirming Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi suffered "far from ideal" injuries in a post-match session on Saturday.

Hincapié was pictured being carried from the pitch by staff during training held at Emirates Stadium after the Gunners beat Leeds United 2-1 last weekend.

Both Hincapié and Zubimendi have suffered ankle injuries and the pair are undergoing scans on Monday to determine the extent of the damage.

Speaking ahead of Tuesday's Champions League home clash with Lille, Arteta said: "We had a training session planned after the game for the players that didn't have enough minutes, to get everybody [into] the recovery on Sunday and to get everybody in the rhythm and in two very unfortunate actions, we lost two players.

"Not great. We need to assess them today, they will have further scans to see how they are and then we will have the timeframe how long they are going to be out for.

"They are both going to miss tomorrow's match, that's for sure. Today they are going to have a further scan and probably tomorrow we will know more and let's see how they are going to go. Piero's one looks a little bit more serious I think but we are going to have to wait and see. [It is] far from ideal."

Such sessions are commonplace and Arteta revealed he had spoken with staff to discuss whether anything could have been done differently to avoid the issues.

"The temptation is now [to say] 'Oh we don't want to take that risk and now we do something else.'

"But we were going to do that the next day anyway and when you play those kind of small-sided games, there is contact and these things can happen. They didn't happen once last season and we did it 37 times I think.

"The fact it is there, people are watching, it raises other doubts. Now it is very difficult to do.

- Arsenal's Jurriën Timber 'happy' with Ben White competition at right-back

- Man City win at angry Anfield; Mourinho overshadows ugly Madrid win

"My question was: If we had to this again the way we planned the seven days that we had in that period with the players that didn't have enough load, would it be the case? The answer is yes. "It is a sport of contact and this can happen. What we can do is guys, they are sop competitive, [say], when we do that, "please don't touch each other too much.' That's it.

"[The solution is] very easy: you don't train. Never train and they don't get injured but the consequence to that is when they have to play, they have no rhythm. When you ask them to play, they are going to have no impact in the game.

"Hopefully it happened now and it doesn't happen again. What can you do? If I knew, I had a crystal ball clear [I'd say] 'Go in the jacuzzi everybody and I'll see you tomorrow.'"

Arteta also confirmed William Saliba has returned to light training but refused to put an exact timeframe on his return to action, confirming the centre-back is still "weeks" away from a comeback.

articles.headline: Arsenal's Gabriel ready to take another penalty despite Champions League final miss
articles.description: Gabriel Magalhães has said he is ready to take another penalty for Arsenal despite his crucial miss in last season's Champions League Final.
articles.body:
Gabriel Magalhães has said he is ready to take another penalty for Arsenal despite his crucial miss in last season's Champions League Final.

Paris Saint-Germain retained Europe's biggest club trophy in May after both Gabriel and Eberechi Eze missed in the shootout at the end of a 1-1 draw in Budapest.

It was the first spot-kick Gabriel had ever taken for Arsenal -- having joined the club in 2020 -- but he vowed he would step up once again if asked in future.

Speaking on Monday ahead of the Gunners' Champions League clash against his former club Lille, Gabriel said: "In the final, anything can happen. We did really well in the Champions League. Of course, if I have another penalty, I'm going to be there to take it.

"My teammates helped me a lot after this. Of course, I was sad, I didn't want to miss a penalty but of course I learn from this and if I have an opportunity, I'm there to take it."

- Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict

- Mikel Arteta defends Arsenal after Piero Hincapié, Martin Zubimendi injuries

Arsenal have never won the Champions League and PSG defender Marquinhos immediately ran to console his Brazil teammate in the immediate aftermath of Gabriel's miss.

"It was brilliant from him to come to me," Gabriel said. "Of course, he missed a penalty in a World Cup and he had a lot of experience for this moment. He said some words to me and helped me a lot.

"After this, I spoke with him as well and I say thank you because in this moment, it was really difficult. He is one of the players I like a lot, I enjoy to play with him when we're at the national team. I learn a lot with him as well. I say thank you to him because it was a [tough] moment for me."

articles.headline: Atlético Madrid's Simeone on Man United: 'They are still creating danger'
articles.description: Atlético Madrid coach Diego Simeone has insisted that Manchester United are still a dangerous opponent despite a run of form which has left the club mid-table in the Premier League.
articles.body:
Atlético Madrid coach Diego Simeone has insisted that Manchester United are still a dangerous opponent despite a run of form which has left the club mid-table in the Premier League.

United were held to a 1-1 draw by struggling, 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford on Saturday to make it four games without a win in the league, with just six points from six games, and growing pressure on manager Michael Carrick.

Atlético host United at the Metropolitano on Tuesday, after an opening round of matches which saw the LaLiga club beaten 2-1 by Liverpool, while United beat Sabah 4-0.

"We face an opponent that applies intense pressure in your half, closing you down quickly, and has players with speed," Simeone said in a news conference on Monday. "Despite their recent results, including a lot of draws, they are still creating the kind of danger that they did last year. They're a strong team."

United qualified for the Champions League after a strong, third-placed finish in the Premier League last season, with Carrick making an impact after replacing Ruben Amorim midway through the campaign.

"Last year in the Premier League, which is the best league in the world, they had a great season," Atlético defender Dávid Hancko said. "There are plenty of positives, even if they haven't started well. They have great players and are undoubtedly a giant. We'll have to play at 100% to win."

Atlético are still waiting for star forward Julián Álvarez to impress this season, after his bid to leave the club in the summer.

Álvarez has failed to score so far, registering just one assist, against Liverpool, after an injury-hit start to 2026-27.

"Forwards with Julián's characteristics always need goals, not just him," Simeone said on Monday.

"Beyond his finishing, he's a team player who links up well with others. He has many more tools in his arsenal than just scoring. He played a great second half the other day [against Alavés] and hopefully he can keep growing to reach the level where we all want to see him."
